questions.question: What is the primary purpose of an investor pitch deck?

options.text: To replace all verbal communication during an investor meeting
To concisely communicate the problem, solution, market, team, and business model to generate investor interest
To list every feature of the product in technical detail
To serve as the final legally binding investment document

questions.explanation: A pitch deck is a storytelling tool that communicates enough for investors to understand the opportunity and decide whether to explore further — not a comprehensive product manual or legal document.

questions.question: Which of the following is a key principle of effective entrepreneurial communication?

options.text: Using maximum technical jargon to demonstrate domain expertise
Tailoring the message to the specific audience and their priorities
Using the same pitch word-for-word with every audience
Avoiding questions from the audience to maintain control

questions.explanation: Effective communication requires understanding who you are addressing. An investor wants ROI and market size; a customer wants the problem solved; an employee wants mission and growth — each needs a tailored message.

questions.question: When pitching to investors, which component of 'value creation potential' is most important to demonstrate?

options.text: The colour scheme and design quality of the pitch deck
A large, growing addressable market combined with a defensible business model
The number of years the founder has worked in unrelated industries
The number of product features relative to competitors

questions.explanation: Investors assess value creation potential through the size and growth of the opportunity and whether the company has or can build a defensible moat — making the return thesis believable.

questions.question: What entrepreneurial lesson does the Airth case study primarily illustrate?

options.text: The importance of operating in sectors with no existing competition
How effective communication of a social impact mission can help attract both customers and investors
Why avoiding media coverage is important for early-stage startups
The futility of pitching to venture capital investors

questions.explanation: Airth demonstrates that clearly communicating a compelling impact mission alongside strong unit economics can differentiate a company and attract mission-aligned investors and customers.

questions.question: A standard investor pitch deck typically includes which of the following elements?

options.text: Full engineering schematics and source code
Problem, solution, market size, business model, traction, team, and funding ask
A comprehensive HR policy manual
Competitor source code and trade secrets

questions.explanation: A strong pitch deck tells a narrative arc: the problem, the solution, the market opportunity, how the business makes money, current traction, the team's credentials, and what funding is sought and for what.

questions.question: What is a '30-second elevator pitch' in the entrepreneurial context?

options.text: A pitch delivered exclusively inside an elevator to building tenants
A very brief, compelling summary of your business that can be delivered in about 30 seconds
A formal 30-minute investor presentation
A video advertisement for social media

questions.explanation: An elevator pitch condenses the essence of a business — the problem, solution, and why it matters — into a short compelling narrative usable in chance networking encounters.

questions.question: Why do investors typically prefer startups addressing a large Total Addressable Market (TAM)?

options.text: Large TAMs are always easier to capture than small ones
A large TAM allows a startup to build a substantial business even if it captures only a small market share
Large markets have less competition by definition
Investors are indifferent between large and small TAMs

questions.explanation: Venture investors need large outcomes to justify their risk. A large TAM means that even capturing 1-5% can produce a billion-dollar company, making the investment thesis viable for fund-level returns.

questions.question: In an investor pitch, 'traction' refers to:

options.text: The physical grip of product packaging on store shelves
Evidence that the market wants the product — such as revenue, users, growth rate, or letters of intent
The founder's personal network size on LinkedIn
The number of patents the company has filed

questions.explanation: Traction is market validation — concrete evidence (revenue, active users, growth metrics, partnerships, LOIs) that proves real demand and reduces investor risk.
